rationale: Start with a broad gradient at an intermediate temperature to locate the elution window for all 10 compounds and identify critical pairs. This leaves ample hold time for late-eluting compounds while establishing a baseline for slope and temperature comparisons.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce run time and measure how the closest pairs respond to gradient steepness. The initial run has sufficient resolution margin to test a substantially faster separation.

Use an intermediate slope to recover resolution in the central cluster without returning to the long baseline run. The large response of the closest pair to gradient duration suggests this is a promising resolution–time compromise.
Test temperature selectivity at the best gradient slope while shortening retention. Higher temperature may separate the remaining critical pair enough to reach full resolution without a time penalty.

Test a modest temperature decrease from the best run to move the central critical pair away from its apparent temperature-driven crossover. The last peak should remain near 9.7 minutes, preserving the zero time penalty while potentially achieving full resolution.

Test just below 60 °C to reopen the newly crowded early pair while retaining the beneficial elution-order change in the central cluster. This temperature should keep the last peak comfortably within the zero-time-penalty window.

Slightly steepen the gradient at the best temperature to improve the central pair, whose elution order appears reversed relative to 40 °C. The other pairs have resolution margin, and the shorter gradient will preserve the zero time penalty.

Injection 7 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the best method. Test a slightly shallower gradient to seek another maximum-score method with a more balanced resolution margin between the two closest pairs.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test a higher starting organic fraction for a faster, equally resolved alternative. Relative to injection 8, this shifts the gradient window upward while preserving its slope, probing selectivity beyond slope changes alone.

Slightly reduce the slope from injection 9 to recover the early critical pair while retaining the improved central-pair separation. This may provide a maximum-score alternative with more balanced resolution margins and no time penalty.

Continue the successful slope adjustment to lift the early critical pair above 1.5 while the central pair retains some margin. The predicted last-peak time remains well within the zero-penalty window, potentially matching the maximum CRF with greater minimum resolution.

The maximum CRF is already achieved; probe a narrower, higher-starting window for greater resolution margin. The shallower slope should protect the early critical pair while the higher starting fraction may improve central-pair selectivity, with all peaks still expected before 10 minutes.

Reduce the slope one grid step from injection 12 to recover the early critical pair while retaining the central pair’s resolution margin. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, offering another route to maximum CRF with improved minimum resolution.

Test one further reduction in slope to improve the early critical pair while the central pair should remain above 1.5. The last peak is expected near 9.8 minutes, potentially preserving maximum CRF with a larger minimum-resolution margin.

Use a slope between injections 13 and 14 to balance their two critical-pair margins while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. This tests another potentially maximum-score method without repeating an existing grid setting.

With maximum CRF already secured, test an alternative at lower temperature using a higher starting fraction to control run time. The shallower slope than injection 3 may resolve its critical central pair while the shifted window offsets increased retention.

Lengthen injection 16’s gradient by one grid step to raise the slope-sensitive central pair above 1.5. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially establishing a maximum-score method at 40 °C.

Shift the starting fraction upward and reduce the slope to seek more central-pair resolution while offsetting the added retention time. Injection 17 already achieves maximum CRF; this tests whether a nearby 40 °C method can match it with greater resolution margin.

Test a slope between injections 13 and 15, where both critical pairs should retain resolution above 1.5 and the last peak should remain below 10 minutes. This targets another maximum-score method with balanced resolution margins; injection 7 remains the fastest demonstrated maximum-score method.

Test a modestly shallower slope than injection 11 to seek another maximum-score method with both critical pairs comfortably above 1.5. This should keep the last peak near 8.2 minutes, offering a shorter alternative to the higher-margin methods starting at 0.15.

Test a slope between injections 10 and 11 to bring both critical pairs above 1.5 while keeping the last peak near 7.8 minutes. This targets a shorter maximum-score alternative to injection 11; the campaign’s maximum CRF is already secured.

Preserve injection 11’s successful gradient slope while trimming the endpoint to just above the last peak’s estimated elution fraction of 0.56. This should retain maximum CRF with all peaks inside the gradient while reducing the programmed gradient duration and final organic strength.

Trim the fastest maximum-score method’s endpoint while preserving injection 7’s slope and temperature. The last peak is expected near 7.6 minutes at an elution fraction around 0.57, safely within this shorter programmed gradient.

Test a trimmed gradient with a slope between injections 13 and 19, targeting balanced critical-pair resolutions around 1.7. The last peak should elute near 9.3 minutes before the gradient ends, preserving maximum CRF with a lower final organic fraction.

Use a slope between injections 24 and 19 to balance the two critical pairs near R = 1.7 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. This final refinement targets maximum CRF with increased resolution margin; injections 7 and 23 remain the fastest demonstrated maximum-score methods.
